clue.text: Hopeless quest: grabbing operagoers' top hats

indicators.note: a hopeless effort is a botched mess, so the following word's letters come out jumbled
to grab something is to hold it within your grasp, so one piece takes another inside it
'top' keeps only the first letter of "operagoers'"

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
the top, or first letter, of operagoers

explanation.surface: A doomed search at the opera house for the hats perched on the audience's heads.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled QUEST wraps around O to make TOQUES.
explanation.definitionFit: A toque is a small brimless hat, also the tall white headgear a chef wears.

clue.text: O'Toole-Hepburn movie in which pride comes after a fall?

definitions.text: in which pride comes after a fall?

blocks.note: first meaning: the 1968 film starring Peter O'Toole and Katharine Hepburn

blocks.clueFragment: in which pride comes after a fall?
blocks.note: second meaning: a pride is a group of lions, and the season after fall (autumn) is the cold one

explanation.walkthrough: The proverb says pride comes before a fall; here pride is a group of lions and fall is autumn, so the season that follows finds them.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1968 film about Henry II and Eleanor of Aquitaine starred O'Toole and Hepburn.

clue.text: Tauter "Dancing Queen" is foremost for ABBA, e.g.

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and change places, so the following word is rearranged
foremost means at the very front, so just the opening letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written
the first letter of Queen

explanation.surface: Praise for the ABBA hit Dancing Queen as the group's tightest song.
explanation.walkthrough: Dancing Queen looks like the song title; split it, as 'Dancing' shuffles the word before it and only Queen's first letter joins.
explanation.definitionFit: ABBA had four members, Agnetha, Björn, Benny and Anni-Frid, so the band is a four-piece group.

clue.text: Getting rid of doctor, men sued to get result

indicators.note: getting rid of something removes it, so those letters are taken out

blocks.note: MD is a doctor of medicine
the two words taken as written; their opening M and closing D are the doctor's letters, so what remains runs unbroken across them, a coincidence of the deletion rather than a hiding

explanation.surface: Patients sacking their physician and suing to win a verdict.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove the M and the D of the doctor from the two words and what is left is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to follow as a consequence, the same as to result.

clue.text: Can she woo? Go crazy

indicators.note: something crazy is out of its right order, so the letters before it are scrambled

blocks.note: the three words taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether a woman can court someone, then urging her to go wild.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Can' reads as a modal verb opening a question, but it is the definition: American slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are American slang words for a jail or prison.

clue.text: Chooses flying spot

indicators.note: letters flying about are scattered and land in new places

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A pilot picks a place to fly to.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to make a choice between alternatives, so opts is a synonym of chooses.

clue.text: Musical TV show is so extremely fashionable

blocks.note: taken as written
ultra means extremely
in means in fashion

explanation.surface: Praise for a music programme on television as terribly trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So extremely' reads as one intensifier but supplies two pieces. Soul Train was a long-running US dance and soul music show.
explanation.definitionFit: Soul Train was the American television programme of soul, R&B and dance music that ran from 1971.

clue.text: Somber expert making a disapproving face

blocks.note: grim means somber and gloomy
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A gloomy specialist pulling a disapproving expression.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted expression of disgust, pain or disapproval.

clue.text: Breaded veal entree wins zilch in contention

indicators.note: contention means strife, letters in conflict jostle into a new order

blocks.note: the three words taken as written

explanation.surface: A veal dish entered in a cooking competition wins nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entree' is part of the cooking story and part of the letters to rearrange, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Wiener schnitzel is the Viennese dish of a thin veal cutlet coated in breadcrumbs and fried.

clue.text: Actress and knight love to rise in time for start of operations

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means going upward, so the letters are read from the bottom
one piece goes in another, so it is placed inside it

blocks.note: D-Day is the military term for the day an operation begins
a knight's title
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: An actress and a knight fall in love just as a big operation begins.
explanation.walkthrough: The knight's title and the zero are reversed together and placed after the first D of D-Day.
explanation.definitionFit: Doris Day was the American singer and film star of Pillow Talk and Calamity Jane.

clue.text: Tests the mornings of yesteryear?

blocks.note: ex- means former
a.m. stands for a morning time, so AMs are mornings

explanation.surface: Wondering whether old exams were simply the mornings of years gone by.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as EX-AMS, former mornings; the question mark flags the playful split.
explanation.definitionFit: Exams are formal tests of knowledge sat by students.

clue.text: Meddlesome, leaderless mob corrupted virtues

indicators.note: without a leader means the first letter is dropped from the next word
corrupted things are spoilt and twisted out of shape, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the word mob with its first letter removed
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A busybody crowd with no one in charge has lost its moral standards.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtrusive behaviour pushes itself into others' business, which is what interfering, meddlesome people do.

clue.text: I printed another way: in bold

indicators.note: doing it another way means arranging the same letters in a different order

blocks.note: the two words taken as written

explanation.surface: A typesetter saying they printed something in a different style, namely boldface type.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bold' looks like the typeface, continuing the printing picture, but it means brave.
explanation.definitionFit: Intrepid means fearless and daring, a synonym of bold in its courageous sense.

clue.text: Fire on retreating barge ultimately breaks wind

indicators.note: something retreating goes back the way it came, so the word is read backwards
'ultimately' keeps only the last letter of 'barge'

blocks.note: a slang verb for breaking wind
the last letter of barge

explanation.surface: A battle on a river, where shooting at a withdrawing barge finally ruptures the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barge ultimately breaks wind' looks like one phrase; split it, as 'breaks wind' is the vulgar word read backwards and the barge gives only its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To strafe is to attack with gunfire, especially from low-flying aircraft, so it means to fire on a target.

clue.text: Marked, like hot coffee?

blocks.note: first meaning: observed or paid attention to
second meaning: hot coffee is served without ice

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals the second reading breaks the word into two: hot coffee is the opposite of the iced kind.
explanation.definitionFit: To mark something is to notice or take heed of it, so marked and noticed are synonyms.

clue.text: Eccentric includes air conditioning in lease

indicators.note: to include something is to hold it inside, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: to charter is to hire or lease
AC is the abbreviation for air conditioning

explanation.surface: An odd tenant insists the rental agreement provide air conditioning.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads backwards: lease includes air conditioning, so the abbreviation sits inside the hire word.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is a colourful, odd person, an eccentric in the noun sense.

clue.text: Artists' underwear

blocks.note: first meaning: people who draw pictures
second meaning: an old word for knickers or underpants

explanation.walkthrough: Read the apostrophe as part of the surface: the first sense is simply the plural noun, artists who draw.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who draw are drawers, and drawers is also a dated term for underpants or long knickers.

clue.text: Veered from detailed uprising, changing 50 to 5

indicators.note: in a down entry rising means going upward, so the letters are read from the bottom
the Roman numeral for fifty is swapped for the numeral for five

blocks.note: taken as written
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Someone strayed from a carefully planned revolt by trading a fifty for a five.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the given word backwards, then swap its L for a V.
explanation.definitionFit: To deviate is to depart from a course, which is to veer away.

clue.text: Part of a plant in New York securing faulty crate

indicators.note: something faulty is defective, so the letters of the next word are out of order
to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so one piece wraps around another

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for New York
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A factory in New York found a broken shipping crate holding plant parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plant' suggests a factory, which matches the crate, but here it is a living plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A nectary is the gland in a flower that secretes nectar, a botanical structure of the plant.

clue.text: Asserted decimal is misaligned

indicators.note: misaligned letters are knocked out of line, so they are put into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone insisted that a decimal point was put in the wrong place.
explanation.definitionFit: To claim is to state firmly that something is true, so claimed is a synonym of asserted.

clue.text: Painter's ride in vehicle with greenish exterior

indicators.note: the exterior of a word is its outside, so only its first and last letters are kept
one piece sits in another, so it is placed inside it

blocks.note: a van is a motor vehicle
a go is a turn on a fairground ride
the outside letters of greenish

explanation.surface: An artist travelling in a car painted a sort of green on the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is short for 'is'. The ride sits inside a pair made of the vehicle plus greenish's outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Vincent van Gogh was the Dutch Post-Impressionist painter of Sunflowers and The Starry Night.

clue.text: Less clear requisite to pop a query

indicators.note: a requisite is a necessary part, so a run of letters is part of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: What's needed before you can put a question is less clear than you thought.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque means hard to see through or understand, so the comparative means murkier, less transparent.

clue.text: Up a tree as part of an improvised performance

definitions.text: as part of an improvised performance

blocks.note: first meaning: stuck in difficulty

blocks.clueFragment: as part of an improvised performance
blocks.note: second meaning: taking part ... session

explanation.walkthrough: A jam is an improvised musical session, so a player taking part is literally in one.
explanation.definitionFit: Being up a tree is an idiom for being stuck with no way out, the same as being in trouble or in difficulty.

clue.text: Bygone memory: the first smoked meat

blocks.note: bygone means past
random-access memory in a computer
I is the Roman numeral for one, the first

explanation.surface: Remembering the first smoked meat someone ever ate, a nostalgic food memory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The first' looks like it qualifies the smoked meat, but it supplies the numeral one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned beef that is cured and smoked, a deli staple.

clue.text: It is like Kyoto, but different!

definitions.text: It is like Kyoto, but different!

indicators.note: a different arrangement of the same city's letters yields another word

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Comparing two Japanese cities: alike in some ways, different in others.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the city made of Kyoto's letters, rearranged, is also a Japanese city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tokyo, the current capital, is a big Japanese city much like Kyoto, the old imperial capital, yet unlike it.

clue.text: White malarkey is on the wane

blocks.note: E. B. White wrote Charlotte's Web
BS is the abbreviation for bullshit, nonsense

explanation.surface: Pale nonsense that is losing its force.
explanation.walkthrough: White is the author E. B. White, whose initials supply the first piece.
explanation.definitionFit: The tide ebbs when it flows out, so to ebb is to decline, to be on the wane.

clue.text: Roster of short-term workers open to being seduced

blocks.note: a temp is a temporary worker
a roster is a table of names and duties

explanation.surface: A rota of temporary staff who are easily lured astray.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'roster of temps', so the pieces join in reverse clue order: a temp table.
explanation.definitionFit: Something temptable can be tempted, lured or enticed, so it is open to seduction.

clue.text: Clumsy person's kindergarten jump

blocks.note: K is the usual US abbreviation for kindergarten, as in K-12
a lutz is a figure-skating jump

explanation.surface: An awkward child's attempt at a hop in the nursery class.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's here is short for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Klutz is American slang, from Yiddish, for an awkward, bumbling person.

clue.text: Humanitarian organization breaking records (Guinness's latest)

indicators.note: breaking something smashes it apart, so its letters are put back together differently

blocks.note: taken as written
the last letter of Guinness

explanation.surface: A charity setting world records, with the Guinness Book of Records noting its newest feat.
explanation.walkthrough: Guinness hints at the record book, but only its final letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Cross is the international movement that provides humanitarian aid in war and disasters.

clue.text: Listen to a piece of vocal music, for example? OK

indicators.note: listening means you go by what you hear, so a word is matched by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: a carol is a song, especially a Christmas one; in American speech the two words sound alike

explanation.surface: Someone asked to listen to a song and say if it is all right.
explanation.walkthrough: OK is not 'all right' here: it names the OK Corral, scene of the 1881 Tombstone gunfight, so OK is an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The OK Corral in Tombstone, Arizona is a famous example of a livestock pen of this kind.
